text:
rachel: quick check — noticed inconsistent behavior when aborting streaming requests across SDKs. Node aborting mid-stream seems to stop tokens but leaves retry middleware kicking in; Go context cancel sometimes leaves goroutine reading the net.Conn. logs: `stream canceled -> retrying` then `write: broken pipe`. anyone seen this?

arjun: yup. Go's context cancellation doesn't automatically close the connection, so if a goroutine is blocked on Read/Write it can leak unless we explicitly cancel the transport or close the stream. usually we do `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` and then ensure transport picks it up. also check `http.Transport.CancelRequest` cases.

kelly: interesting — on Node we use AbortController and fetch; when `controller.abort()` happens fetch rejects with an AbortError but our retry layer catches all network errors and retries. we need a retry predicate that treats abort as terminal. filing notes: change `shouldRetry(err)` to return false for abort errors.

sam: i've got a small PR that adds `isAbortError` checks to the retry guard in the JS SDK. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1423 — pls review. also added a unit that simulates abort during streaming to ensure no extra retries.

infra-bot: CI passed for PR 1423 — all checks green (:white_check_mark:)

arjun: THANKS sam. for Go, i can add an integration test that spawns a server that closes the connection when ctx canceled and assert our client goroutine exits. should we also set a standardized error `errors.Aborted` across SDKs? would help higher layers.

rachel: yes please. unify the error code/symbol across SDKs. consumer-facing invariant: abort => immediate terminal aborted error, no retries, no automatic fallback. also for streaming: ensure any local buffers/tokens are discarded (don't attempt to flush).

kelly: agreed. proposal: map Node `AbortError`, Go `context.Canceled`, Python `asyncio.CancelledError` to `errors.Aborted` with code `ABORTED` in our response error model. PR checklist: docs + changelog + cross-sdk integration test.

sam: noted the edge case where network errors and ctx cancel race and we sometimes surface `broken pipe` instead of `ABORTED`. plan: if ctx.Done() is closed within 50ms of socket error, translate to ABORTED in transport layer. want opinions.

arjun: fine by me. implement in transport: if ctx.Err() != nil then wrap as `errors.Aborted("context canceled")`. small safeguard: only wrap if ctx.Deadline not exceeded? hmm. leaning to always map cancellation to ABORTED.

rachel: sounds good. who wants to own cross-sdk issue and coord PRs? i'll send a follow-up ticket but need volunteers to shepherd.

arjun: i'll take Go and coord with infra to add the integration test harness.

kelly: i'll take Node. question tho — should we try to flush buffered tokens before returning ABORTED? i think no; abort should be immediate. :+1:

sam: i'll update retry middleware in Python and Node to check for abort semantics. will add tests.

rachel: cool. i'll open the umbrella ticket and link PRs. ping me when PRs are ready for cross-review. also cc @pr-bot for auto-assign.

pr-bot: assigning PR 1423 to @rachel for follow-up review and linking new ticket #3327 (cancel-semantics-unify).

arjun: one more note — add a stress test that cancels mid-prefix-cache warmup to ensure no KV leaks. found one leak last sprint.

kelly: thanks, adding to checklist. i'll drop a short code sample in the Node PR showing proper AbortController usage:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
client.stream({ prompt: 'hi' }, { signal: ac.signal })
  .on('data', chunk => { /*...*/ })
  .on('end', () => console.log('ended'))
  .on('error', e => console.error('err', e.code || e.message));
// cancel after 200ms
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 200);
```

rachel: perfect. thanks everyone — i'll post the ticket and timeline. expect a sync in tomorrow's devex standup for blockers.
